subject.title: fix(security): add ReDoS guard to exec approval argPattern matching

question: When Doctor finds an existing unsafe exec-approval `argPattern`, should `openclaw doctor --fix` remove that allowlist entry fail-closed and report it, or should maintainers choose a different explicit remediation contract?
rationale: The guard intentionally changes the effect of persisted approval policy, while automatically broadening an entry by dropping only `argPattern` would weaken the security boundary.

options.title: Remove unsafe entries fail-closed
options.body: Have Doctor remove each unsafe allowlist entry, report the affected executable and pattern, and require an operator to recreate a safe rule.

options.title: Diagnose without automatic repair
options.body: Keep the runtime rejection but have Doctor only report actionable repair instructions, accepting that old policy files remain invalid until edited.

recommendation.title: Remove unsafe entries fail-closed
recommendation.body: Have Doctor remove each unsafe allowlist entry, report the affected executable and pattern, and require an operator to recreate a safe rule.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the current allowlist argument-pattern behavior and is the strongest history-based routing candidate for its upgrade contract.
